name: Equine Reverie
intro: Follow the rider, mane and lifted legs around a sculptural form. Rotate slowly to see where the silhouette opens up.
note: A lighter study of the supplied sculpture, scaled to a 100 mm maximum extent.
lesson: Drag the model to compare its front and three-quarter silhouette.
Turn on mesh view to see how triangles describe the mane and limbs.
Open the matching Form project. Select the mesh to explore sculpt brushes and editable modifiers.
shots: A front-facing shaded view of the imported sculpture in Form.
The same mesh in Form’s orthographic Technical view.
An isometric Rendered view reveals the volume behind the silhouette.

name: Circle of Anarchy
intro: A ring of figures becomes a study in repetition, depth and open space. Inspect the center, then look along the edge.
note: Prepared from the supplied high-detail OBJ. This downloadable study contains mesh geometry, not a parametric CAD history.
lesson: Choose Front to read the ring and the spaces between the figures.
Rotate to the side to inspect the relief’s thickness.
Download the Form project, then use its mesh export controls to explore OBJ, PLY or STL handoff.
shots: The imported circular sculpture in Form’s Shaded view.
Technical mode makes a useful companion to the perspective view.
An angled Rendered view shows the sculpture’s shallow depth.

name: Birds in Orbit
intro: Explore the feather edges, crossed bars and circular frame of the supplied bird-and-cross model.
note: Display title for the supplied wwspc model. Fine details are simplified in this web study; the source file remains unchanged.
lesson: Use Front to compare the birds against the circular frame.
Zoom in, then switch to Mesh to inspect the simplified feather geometry.
Open the Form project and compare Shaded, Technical and Rendered viewport modes.
shots: A shaded front view of the bird-and-cross relief inside Form.
The same imported relief shown in Technical mode.
The angled view separates wings, frame and cross in depth.

name: Terrain Study
intro: Look across the ridges, then move overhead to understand how the terrain’s surfaces fit together.
note: Terrain geometry extracted from the supplied FBX. Sky dome and texture-based tree cards are omitted. Textures are not imported into this Form study.
lesson: Choose Angle to read the height changes across the terrain.
Switch to Top and Mesh to inspect the surface layout.
Download the prepared OBJ and import it through Form’s Sculpt panel with units set to mm.
shots: The converted terrain geometry in Form’s isometric Shaded view.
An orthographic Technical view of the landscape study.
Form’s Top view reveals the footprint of the terrain pieces.
